metrics.name: modularity
metrics.feedback: Only main() is defined. Extract a helper function (e.g., add(long long, long long)).

suggestions: Handle overflow explicitly with a wider integer type (e.g. long long) or check b <= INT_MAX - a.
Add function prototypes/headers and avoid placing all logic into a single monolithic block.
Extract helper function (e.g., int add(int a, int b)) into its own function; call it from main.
Rename single-letter variables (e.g., a, b to num1, num2); add descriptive comments.

usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate submissions for an 'add two integers safely' task. The agent ranks them by correctness, edge-case handling, and memory safety, and gives an explainable per-metric score.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering where every rejection can be justified metric by metric.

usefulness.use_case: Plagiarism and LLM-copy triage for instructors
usefulness.example: Two submissions reach a similarity of 0.93 against the 0.85 threshold, so the agent raises a flag in the report. The instructor reviews only those pairs instead of all 300.
usefulness.benefit: Saves review time by narrowing manual checking to suspicious cases.

usefulness.use_case: Automated lab assignment grading in university courses
usefulness.example: In a course of 300 students submitting weekly assignments, the agent validates correctness, enforces modularity rules, and flags infinite loops unattended.
usefulness.benefit: Eliminates TA grading fatigue and guarantees consistent, reproducible scoring across all submissions.

usefulness.example: Junior developers submit pull requests for embedded systems. The agent automatically checks static complexity, compiler warnings, and sanitizer bounds before merging.
usefulness.benefit: Prevents memory leaks, buffer overruns, and style regressions from entering production branches.

limitations.example: A submission passes all 10 hidden tests but fails when the input has extra whitespace or a trailing newline that no test covers. The agent still reports 10/10.
limitations.mitigation: The agent should create its own extra tricky test inputs and compare the student's answers with the answers of a correct program.

limitations.limitation: Empirical complexity estimation is sensitive to OS scheduler noise
limitations.example: Under heavy background CPU load, an O(1) submission may exhibit variable execution times across sizes, risking false classification as non-constant time.
limitations.mitigation: Combine empirical wall-clock timing with static AST loop/recursion analysis and instruction-count profiling.

limitations.limitation: Token similarity can miss obfuscated plagiarism
limitations.example: A student renames identifiers, reorders independent statements, and inserts dummy functions, reducing token similarity below 0.85 despite copied logic.
limitations.mitigation: Integrate AST subgraph isomorphism and semantic control-flow graph (CFG) analysis alongside token matching.

limitations.limitation: Non-deterministic LLM feedback across different local or cloud models
limitations.example: Different LLMs or varying temperature parameters might judge variable naming or comments with different leniency, violating grading reproducibility.
limitations.mitigation: Fix LLM temperature to 0.0 with a static seed, and enforce a rule-based deterministic static rubric fallback.
